title: Episode 70 — Slink Johnson and the Return Guest
summary: Slink Johnson discusses Lamar Davis in Grand Theft Auto V, Black Jesus, The Boondocks, Too $hort, comedy, school service, adult-film production, graffiti, and the path from class clown to working entertainer. His substantial creative history is repeatedly compressed into racial and sexual stereotypes. The longer second movement brings back a nineteen-year-old audience participant after the show posted her photograph and sexual disclosures. The cast speculates about diagnoses, catalogs her body and sexual history, pitches men as candidates, displays explicit media, and stages a long fantasy. The record preserves these actions as evidence of group, celebrity, age, recording, and publication power; it does not reproduce the young guest as a searchable sexual dossier. Her refusals remain authoritative. Later STI and yeast-infection claims receive current health corrections, while private partners, customers, residences, schools, families, explicit images, and operational details stay withheld.
sensitivity: Racial and ethnic slurs and stereotypes; explicit sexual content; young-adult sexual disclosure and group pressure; speculative diagnoses; public image and identity solicitation; anatomy, virginity, orientation and age misinformation; explicit-image display and private partner media; pornography and performer pressure; drug use, gambling and criminal history; STI and yeast-infection misinformation; workplace and customer boundaries; family sexualization; nonconsensual touching and imposed bodily-contact game.
speaker_policy: Named dialogue remains withheld. Episode 70 has zero diarized turns and five coarse window embeddings for a large ensemble. Public guests and cast are contextually known, but no independently held-out multispeaker validation has passed.
